title: Media Links Brings Ultra Resilient IP Transport Proven at the World’s Biggest Live Sports Events to NAB 2026
body_html:
What Was Announced

Media Links has announced the introduction of its ultra-resilient IP transport solution, proven in the world's biggest live sports events, at NAB 2026. This development is significant as it addresses the need for reliable and efficient IP-based transport of high-quality video and audio signals in live broadcast environments. By showcasing this solution at NAB, Media Links aims to demonstrate its capabilities in supporting the demanding requirements of live sports broadcasting, where signal integrity and reliability are paramount.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The introduction of Media Links' ultra-resilient IP transport solution has substantial implications for broadcast engineers and operators, as it promises to enhance the reliability and efficiency of IP-based signal transport. This solution is likely to be of particular interest to those responsible for designing and operating IP-based broadcast infrastructures, where the ability to maintain signal integrity and minimize downtime is critical. By providing a proven solution for resilient IP transport, Media Links is addressing a key challenge in the transition from traditional SDI-based infrastructures to more flexible and scalable IP-based architectures. The use of standards such as SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 is likely to be a key factor in the solution's ability to integrate with existing broadcast systems and workflows.

The solution's ability to support the transport of high-quality video and audio signals over IP networks will be of particular interest to those involved in live sports broadcasting, where the need for reliable and low-latency signal transport is especially critical. The use of IP-based transport also enables the use of more flexible and scalable signal routing and switching architectures, which can help to reduce the complexity and cost of broadcast infrastructures. Furthermore, the solution's support for standards such as SMPTE ST 2110 will facilitate the integration of IP-based signal transport with existing broadcast systems and workflows, including those using SDI and AES67.

Industry Context

The introduction of Media Links' ultra-resilient IP transport solution reflects the ongoing trend towards the adoption of IP-based architectures in the broadcast industry. As broadcasters increasingly seek to take advantage of the flexibility and scalability of IP-based infrastructures, the need for reliable and efficient IP-based signal transport has become a key challenge. The use of standards such as SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 has helped to facilitate the transition to IP-based architectures, and the development of solutions such as Media Links' ultra-resilient IP transport will be critical in supporting the widespread adoption of these standards. The broadcast industry's shift towards IP-based architectures is also being driven by the need to support new formats and services, such as UHD and HDR, which require higher bandwidth and more flexible signal transport.

The development of IP-based signal transport solutions is also being influenced by the growing use of cloud-based services and virtualized architectures in the broadcast industry. The use of cloud-based services and virtualized architectures requires the ability to transport high-quality video and audio signals over IP networks, and the development of solutions such as Media Links' ultra-resilient IP transport will be critical in supporting the widespread adoption of these technologies. Furthermore, the use of IP-based signal transport will also facilitate the integration of broadcast systems with other IP-based services, such as OTT and CDN, which are becoming increasingly important in the delivery of broadcast content to consumers.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

The introduction of Media Links' ultra-resilient IP transport solution has significant implications for broadcast and media teams, particularly those involved in live sports broadcasting and the design and operation of IP-based broadcast infrastructures. Engineers and operators should take note of the solution's ability to provide reliable and efficient IP-based signal transport, and its potential to support the transition to more flexible and scalable IP-based architectures. The solution's support for standards such as SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 will also facilitate the integration of IP-based signal transport with existing broadcast systems and workflows, making it easier to deploy and manage IP-based infrastructures.

As the broadcast industry continues to evolve towards more IP-based architectures, the development of solutions such as Media Links' ultra-resilient IP transport will be critical in supporting the widespread adoption of these technologies.
